message.content:
{
  "summary": "Glial cells support neural signaling by regulating extracellular environments and forming myelin; myelination enables rapid saltatory conduction while unmyelinated axons remain functional, and myelin damage impairs conduction without necessarily destroying neurons.",
  "topics": [
    "Astrocytes regulate extracellular chemical environment including potassium levels",
    "Oligodendrocytes form myelin in the central nervous system",
    "Schwann cells form myelin in the peripheral nervous system",
    "One oligodendrocyte myelinates segments of several axons versus one Schwann cell per segment",
    "Myelin increases electrical insulation between nodes of Ranvier for rapid saltatory conduction",
    "Unmyelinated axons can still conduct signals",
    "Damage to myelin slows or causes conduction failure without destroying the neuron"
  ]
}
